project.name: Hark
project.description: Hark is a local-first, macOS-only meeting transcription app that delivers live captions, translation, and offline speaker diarization with WhisperKit on-device ASR, writing markdown notes to a user-owned vault — no cloud speech-to-text, no account, and no telemetry. It pairs a Swift sidecar daemon (harkd) for audio capture, transcription, and diarization with an Electron + Angular 21 desktop UI.

nodes.name: app.component.ts
nodes.summary: Root Angular component for the Hark UI: orchestrates capture controls, the live transcript view, all overlay panels (settings, summary, translate, speaker tagging, post-meeting review), and the ask-meeting/ask-vault flows by wiring together the engine, LLM, preferences and retrieval services.
nodes.languageNotes: Standalone Angular component using signals heavily for reactive state; a single ~900-line class with ~50 methods coordinating capture, transcript, panels and Electron tray bridge (window.hark).

nodes.name: AppComponent
nodes.summary: The top-level application component holding all global UI state (connection, capture, segments, panels) and exposing handlers for starting/stopping capture, bookmarking, tagging speakers, asking the meeting or vault, and managing summary/translation/review overlays.

nodes.name: Diarizer.swift

nodes.name: EmbedderModels.swift
nodes.summary: Curated, local-only registry of 384-dim text-embedding models for vault RAG (ADR-0032); pure config records with no behavior, loading lives in EmbedderLoader.

nodes.name: EngineSession.swift
nodes.summary: harkd's central transcription session actor wiring Capture → VAD → SlidingWindow → WhisperKit → WebSocket emit, with backpressure, dedup, diarization, and vault save lifecycle.

nodes.name: HarkdCommand.swift
nodes.summary: harkd daemon entry point: binds the WebSocket server and writes the engine.port file first, then loads WhisperKit behind it and waits for shutdown signals.

nodes.name: RagChunker.swift
nodes.summary: Stateless, heading-aware markdown chunker that splits a vault note into overlapping embeddable windows with breadcrumb prefixes, lifting YAML front-matter into metadata.

nodes.name: RagIndex.swift
nodes.summary: Brute-force in-memory cosine vector store for vault RAG, persisted as a flat file set; an actor serializing the background indexer and foreground retrieve query path.

nodes.name: RagIndexer.swift
nodes.summary: Vault-RAG index coordinator: cold build on open, FSEvents-driven debounced re-index, manual rebuild, and graceful degradation when the embedder is unavailable.

nodes.name: SlidingWindow.swift
nodes.summary: Speech-gated 30 s/5 s-hop sliding window plus the UtteranceLedger that reconciles re-transcribed segments into stable utterance identities (ADR-0008/0009/0019).

nodes.name: SpeakerEnrollment.swift
nodes.summary: Local voiceprint store and matcher (ADR-0026): persists a named speaker's diarizer centroid and auto-recognizes that voice in future meetings via cosine distance.

nodes.name: TextEmbedder.swift
nodes.summary: On-device CoreML text embedder for vault RAG: tokenize, ANE inference, masked mean-pooling over real tokens, and L2-normalize to a 384-dim vector, fully offline.

nodes.name: VAD.swift
nodes.summary: Voice Activity Detection protocol plus an initial energy-based implementation with hangover, gating which audio frames accumulate into the sliding window.

nodes.name: VaultWriter.swift
nodes.summary: Stateless writer that renders a finished meeting to vault markdown (front-matter + blockquoted utterances) and git-commits it, invoked only at capture.stop.

nodes.name: WebSocketServer.swift

nodes.name: WireProtocol.swift
nodes.summary: JSON envelope and Codable payload structs for the harkd↔UI WebSocket API, defining every engine→UI event and UI→engine command in the wire contract.

nodes.name: HarkEngine.swift
nodes.summary: hark-engine Phase 1 batch transcription CLI: runs WhisperKit on an audio file and emits structured JSON segments matching the WebSocket segment.final shape.

nodes.summary: Placeholder test target stub that lets HarkCaptureTests compile before the per-component capture tests land.

nodes.name: WAVWriterTests.swift
nodes.summary: Round-trip tests for HarkCore.WAVWriter verifying PCM samples survive a write/read cycle.

nodes.name: AudioPersistenceTests.swift
nodes.summary: Coverage for opt-in meeting-audio persistence and the keep_audio privacy gate (ADR-0027), driving the production AudioStore against a temp .audio dir.

nodes.name: CommitWatermarkTests.swift
nodes.summary: Regression coverage for ADR-0019's region-based commit-watermark finalization, proving each audio region finalizes exactly once despite ~6× re-transcription.

nodes.name: DedupTests.swift
nodes.summary: Regression coverage for EngineSession.collapseReemissions: the at-stop, interval-based, time-gated collapse of re-emitted utterances that preserves far-apart repeats.

nodes.name: EmbedderTests.swift
nodes.summary: Coverage for the vault-RAG text embedder (ADR-0032): pure pipeline math (masked pooling, L2-normalize, prefixes) plus gated on-device cross-lingual sanity checks.

nodes.name: MeetingTranscriptTests.swift
nodes.summary: Coverage for the meeting.transcript mapping (EngineSession.transcriptUtterances) that carries deduped, speaker-labeled vault utterances back to the on-screen UI.

nodes.name: AudioStore
nodes.summary: Sendable struct that atomically writes the in-RAM meeting PCM to vault/.audio/<id>.wav, returning nil and doing zero I/O when keep_audio is off.

nodes.name: Diarizer
nodes.summary: Actor confining FluidAudio's OfflineDiarizerManager so its heavyweight CoreML model state is touched from exactly one isolation domain.

nodes.name: EmbedderModels
nodes.summary: Enum-backed registry exposing the curated local embedding models and the default selection used by the indexer and loader.

nodes.name: EngineSession
nodes.summary: Core session actor owning the full transcription lifecycle: ingest, VAD gating, windowed WhisperKit jobs with single-flight backpressure, reconciliation, dedup, diarization, and vault save.

nodes.name: HarkdCommand
nodes.summary: AsyncParsableCommand that boots the daemon: binds the WS server, writes the port file, loads WhisperKit behind it, and blocks on shutdown signals.

nodes.name: ModelProgressThrottle
nodes.summary: Rate-limits model-load progress callbacks so download/compile progress emits to clients without flooding the WebSocket.

nodes.name: RagChunker
nodes.summary: Stateless enum namespace whose pure chunk method turns one markdown note into heading-aware overlapping windows with breadcrumb prefixes and lifted metadata.

nodes.name: RagIndex
nodes.summary: Actor vector store holding the normalized 384-dim matrix and metadata, serving brute-force cosine search and persisting/loading the flat on-disk index.

nodes.name: RagIndexer

nodes.summary: Bridges the C FSEvents stream onto a dedicated DispatchQueue and surfaces coalesced vault change callbacks to the indexer.

nodes.name: UtteranceLedger
nodes.summary: Reconciles each re-transcribed window against prior emissions using overlap-based identity and a monotonic commit watermark so each region finalizes exactly once.

nodes.name: SlidingWindowBuffer
nodes.summary: Accumulates VAD-gated speech frames into a 30 s window and pops a 5 s hop when ready to drive the next transcription pass.

nodes.name: SpeakerStore
nodes.summary: Sendable struct over a directory of speaker JSON files: enrolls a named voiceprint centroid and matches future diarizer centroids by cosine distance.

nodes.name: CoreMLTextEmbedder
nodes.summary: Actor implementing the TextEmbedder protocol: tokenizes with e5 prefixes, runs ANE inference, masked-mean-pools over real tokens, and L2-normalizes to 384-dim.

nodes.name: TextEmbedder
nodes.summary: Protocol abstracting a string-to-normalized-vector embedder so the RAG index and indexer depend on the interface, not the CoreML implementation.

nodes.name: EnergyVAD
nodes.summary: Energy-based VAD with hangover: classifies 100 ms RMS frames through a silence/speech state machine to gate the sliding window.

nodes.name: VAD
nodes.summary: Protocol defining the voice-activity-detection interface so the energy gate can be swapped for a Silero CoreML implementation later.

nodes.name: VaultWriter
nodes.summary: Sendable struct that renders a finished meeting to vault markdown with front-matter and blockquoted utterances, then git-commits it at capture.stop.

nodes.name: HarkdWebSocketServer
nodes.summary: SwiftNIO server that binds loopback, performs WebSocket upgrades, tracks clients, and broadcasts wire frames with periodic heartbeats.

nodes.name: HarkdWSAppHandler
nodes.summary: NIO channel handler decoding inbound JSON frames and forwarding outbound wire messages between a connected client and the delegate.

nodes.name: WebSocketClient
nodes.summary: Represents one connected WebSocket client, holding its channel and identity for targeted and broadcast frame delivery.

nodes.name: HarkEngineCommand
nodes.summary: AsyncParsableCommand for hark-engine: parses args, runs WhisperKit on an input file, and emits structured JSON segments to stdout or a file.

nodes.name: EmbedderModel
nodes.summary: Immutable descriptor for one embedding model: id, revision, dimension, tokenizer family, and CoreML/tokenizer cache paths.

nodes.name: ModelProgressTests.swift
nodes.summary: XCTest suite pinning the first-run model-load progress path: the pure ModelProgressThrottle.decide rate-limiter (never drops a phase transition) and the MetaModelProgressPayload wire encoding (indeterminate fraction serializes as JSON null, not a dropped key).
nodes.languageNotes: Drives the pure decide() with injected now/lastEmitAt so the time branch is deterministic; asserts on encodeWireMessage output directly.

nodes.name: RagChunkerTests.swift
nodes.summary: XCTest suite for the vault-RAG markdown chunker (ADR-0032/0033): front-matter stripped to metadata and not embedded, heading-aware breadcrumb windows, overlapping splits for long sections, and stable content-addressed chunk ids.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure value-to-value chunker driven with literal synthetic markdown; no embedder or filesystem so it always runs.

nodes.name: RagIndexerTests.swift
nodes.summary: XCTest suite for the vault-RAG indexer coordinator (ADR-0032/0033): cold build, content-hash skip gate, incremental change/delete handling, graceful degradation without an embedder, and the offset-only retrieve path that recovers text live from the vault.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a deterministic FNV-1a FakeEmbedder conforming to TextEmbedder and a unique temp vault/index dir per test; never touches the real vault.

nodes.name: RagIndexTests.swift
nodes.summary: XCTest suite for the vault-RAG vector index (ADR-0032/0033): brute-force cosine top-K ranking, persist/reload round-trip of textless metadata, model-id/revision-change rebuild, and incremental replaceFile row swapping.
nodes.languageNotes: Feeds synthetic L2-normalized vectors directly into the actor index; asserts the offset-only meta.jsonl never persists raw note text.

nodes.name: RagWireTests.swift
nodes.summary: XCTest suite pinning the exact snake_case wire shapes for the vault-RAG frames (rag.retrieve, rag.results, rag.index_status) so the TypeScript UI contract can be written against assertions rather than guesswork.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure encode/decode round-trips via decodeInbound/encodeWireMessage; pins field names and null handling.

nodes.name: SpeakerEnrollmentTests.swift
nodes.summary: XCTest suite for the local voiceprint store and matcher (SpeakerStore) plus env-threshold parse/clamp (ADR-0026), driving the production store against a temp .speakers/ dir.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses synthetic float vectors only (never real voice data) and points the store at a per-test temp root; imports FluidAudio.

nodes.name: SpeakerRenameTests.swift
nodes.summary: Regression suite for the post-save speaker-rename relabel + re-render path (EngineSession.applySpeakerNames + VaultWriter.renderMarkdown), driving the production functions directly so the live speaker.rename path and tests share one definition.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure label-mapping (applySpeakerNames) plus markdown re-render assertions; no reimplementation of production logic.

nodes.name: SummaryWriteTests.swift
nodes.summary: XCTest suite for the summary.write persistence path (VaultWriter.mergeSummarySection + appendSummary) and the SummaryWriteCommand wire decode (ADR-0031), verifying pure read-modify-write of a `## Summary` section into the saved meeting markdown.
nodes.languageNotes: Exercises the section merge purely plus a filesystem read-modify-write against a temp file; git commit is best-effort and not asserted.

nodes.name: TranslationWriteTests.swift
nodes.summary: XCTest suite for the translation.write persistence path (VaultWriter.mergeTranslationSection + appendTranslation) and the TranslationWriteCommand wire decode, pinning that per-language `## Transcript — <lang>` sections coexist and re-translating one language replaces only that section.
nodes.languageNotes: Largest suite in the batch; the critical property is the exact language-qualified heading match so independent language sections never clobber each other.

nodes.name: UtteranceLedgerTests.swift
nodes.summary: Regression suite for the UtteranceLedger overlap-based identity rule (ADR-0009), reproducing the 2026-05-28 smoke-trace engulfment bug where a coarse new segment wrongly reassigned a short utterance's id.
nodes.languageNotes: Numbers are taken verbatim from a real smoke trace; pins overlap / max(longer) >= 0.5 as the reassignment threshold.

nodes.languageNotes: Extends colors/fontFamily/borderRadius with var(--token) references rather than literal values; content globs scan ./src for html and ts.

nodes.name: harkd-spawn.ts
nodes.summary: Spawns and supervises the harkd Swift sidecar child process from the Electron main process, resolving the signed binary path and waiting on the port file before reporting readiness.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Promise.race against the spawned child's exit to fail fast if harkd crashes during startup.

nodes.name: resolveBinaryPath
nodes.summary: Resolves the harkd binary location by probing packaged-app and dev candidate paths and returning the first that exists on disk.

nodes.name: spawnHarkd
nodes.summary: Launches the harkd sidecar, races startup against an early-exit/port-file timeout, and returns a handle exposing the resolved port and a graceful stop function.

nodes.name: main.ts
nodes.summary: Electron main-process entry point: bootstraps the app, ensures the vault directory, spawns harkd, creates the main BrowserWindow and the menu-bar tray, and wires the IPC handlers that bridge the renderer to prefs, the LLM layer, and RAG retrieval.
nodes.languageNotes: Persists window bounds with a debounced save and validates restored geometry against the current display set before reuse.

nodes.name: createWindow
nodes.summary: Constructs the main BrowserWindow with the secure preload, restores persisted bounds, loads the renderer, and registers window lifecycle listeners that sync tray state and persist geometry.

nodes.name: resolveInitialBounds
nodes.summary: Loads persisted window bounds and returns them only if they still fall on a connected display, otherwise falls back to default geometry.

nodes.name: bootstrap
nodes.summary: App startup sequence that ensures the vault directory, spawns the harkd sidecar, then creates the main window and tray.

nodes.name: createTray
nodes.summary: Instantiates the menu-bar tray and its popover, wiring tray actions and toggle handlers back into window and renderer messaging.

nodes.name: isRectOnSomeDisplay
nodes.summary: Checks whether a stored window rectangle still overlaps any currently attached display so off-screen geometry is not restored.

nodes.name: port-file.ts
nodes.summary: Reads and polls the harkd port file (the sidecar writes its listening port as JSON), exposing a path resolver and an await-with-timeout helper used during engine startup.

nodes.name: waitForPortFile
nodes.summary: Polls for the harkd port file until it appears and parses, or rejects after the configured timeout.

nodes.name: readPortFile
nodes.summary: Reads and JSON-parses the harkd port file, returning the listening port or null if it is missing or malformed.

nodes.name: prefs.ts
nodes.summary: Loads, sanitizes, and atomically persists user preferences (theme, privacy flags, window bounds, LLM and RAG backend config) to the app-support directory, with defensive validation of every untrusted field.
nodes.languageNotes: Atomic save via temp-file write plus rename; every nested section has a dedicated sanitizer that rejects malformed input rather than trusting the JSON.

nodes.name: savePrefs
nodes.summary: Merges a partial prefs patch over the current prefs, sanitizes the result, and writes it atomically via a temp file and rename.

nodes.name: loadPrefs
nodes.summary: Reads the prefs file from disk, parses and sanitizes it, and falls back to defaults when the file is missing or corrupt.

nodes.name: sanitize
nodes.summary: Top-level prefs sanitizer that coerces each section (theme, privacy, window, LLM, RAG) through its dedicated validator, dropping unknown or invalid fields.

nodes.name: sanitizeRag
nodes.summary: Validates the RAG backend section, normalizing transport, trimmed endpoint, and tool name for an external retrieval backend.

nodes.name: sanitizeWindow
nodes.summary: Validates persisted window-bounds prefs, accepting only finite positive dimensions and finite coordinates.

nodes.name: preload.ts
nodes.summary: Electron preload script that exposes the sandboxed window.hark API to the renderer via contextBridge, bridging engine port lookup, tray state, prefs, vault reveal, mic permission, and the LLM/RAG IPC channels under contextIsolation.
nodes.languageNotes: Trust boundary: a TRAY_ACTIONS whitelist gates forwarded actions, and array args are filtered before crossing contextBridge per ADR-0001's security model.

nodes.name: http.ts
nodes.summary: Plain-HTTP transport for the external RAG retrieval backend, issuing loopback POST requests with abort-timeout handling and mapping fetch failures to content-free error verdicts.

nodes.name: httpRetrieve
nodes.summary: Performs a POST retrieve query against the loopback HTTP backend with an abort timeout and coerces the untrusted response into retrieved chunks.

nodes.name: httpTestConnection
nodes.summary: Probes the loopback HTTP retrieval backend with a canned query and returns a one-line content-free connection verdict.

nodes.name: mapFetchError
nodes.summary: Translates raw fetch/abort errors into user-facing, content-free error detail strings for retrieval failures.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Facade for the external RAG retrieval feature: reads backend config from prefs, enforces loopback-only endpoints, clamps the result count, and dispatches retrieve/testConnection to the HTTP or MCP transport.
nodes.languageNotes: Re-exports the public RAG types alongside the dispatch functions, acting as the module's single entry surface.

nodes.name: retrieve
nodes.summary: Reads RAG config, validates the loopback endpoint, clamps k, and routes the query to the MCP or HTTP transport, mapping results into renderer-shaped chunks.

nodes.name: testConnection
nodes.summary: Reads RAG config, enforces loopback, and delegates a connection probe to the configured MCP or HTTP transport.

nodes.name: loopback.ts
nodes.summary: Privacy guard that asserts a configured RAG endpoint resolves to a loopback host before any fetch, enforcing ADR-0034's rule that vault retrieval traffic never leaves the machine.

nodes.name: assertLoopbackEndpoint
nodes.summary: Parses an endpoint URL and throws unless its host is a recognized loopback address, blocking any non-local retrieval target.

nodes.name: mcp.ts
nodes.summary: Minimal MCP-over-Streamable-HTTP client for the external RAG backend, hand-rolling JSON-RPC handshake, tool calls, and SSE response extraction with no SDK per ADR-0029.
nodes.languageNotes: Parses both plain JSON and SSE 'data:' framed JSON-RPC responses, extracting tool text content from the MCP result envelope.

nodes.name: rpc
nodes.summary: Issues a single JSON-RPC request over Streamable HTTP with an abort timeout, parsing either a JSON or SSE-framed response into a typed RPC result.

nodes.name: mcpRetrieve
nodes.summary: Performs the MCP handshake then calls the configured search tool, coercing the returned tool JSON into retrieved chunks.

nodes.name: mcpTestConnection
nodes.summary: Handshakes and lists MCP tools to verify the configured search tool exists, returning a content-free connection verdict.

nodes.name: handshake
nodes.summary: Performs the MCP initialize exchange and fires the initialized notification to open a usable session.

nodes.name: extractRpcFromSse
nodes.summary: Scans an SSE event stream for the data line carrying the JSON-RPC response matching the requested id.

nodes.name: extractToolJson
nodes.summary: Pulls the text content out of an MCP tool-call result envelope and parses it into JSON.

nodes.name: parse.ts
nodes.summary: Defensively coerces untrusted external-backend retrieval responses into well-formed RetrievedChunk objects, discarding malformed entries.

nodes.name: coerceExternalChunks
nodes.summary: Validates an untrusted backend response array and maps each well-formed entry to a normalized RetrievedChunk, dropping anything malformed.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Type definitions for the external RAG retrieval backend: transport selection, backend config mirroring prefs, retrieved-chunk shapes, and connection-result verdicts.

nodes.name: tray-popover.ts
nodes.summary: Manages the borderless menu-bar tray popover BrowserWindow, handling lazy window creation, anchored positioning near the tray icon, show/hide/toggle, and pushing capture state to its renderer.

nodes.name: TrayPopover
nodes.summary: Encapsulates the tray popover window: lazily builds a borderless always-on-top BrowserWindow, computes a position anchored to the tray icon, and toggles/pushes state to it.

nodes.name: tray.ts
nodes.summary: Builds the macOS menu-bar tray icon and context menu, swapping template images between idle and recording states and dispatching tray actions (start/stop, show window, quit) to main-process callbacks.
nodes.languageNotes: Decodes base64-embedded 1x/2x template PNGs into a single nativeImage so the tray icon adapts to light/dark menu bars.

nodes.name: HarkTray
nodes.summary: Owns the menu-bar Tray instance: sets idle/recording template icons, rebuilds the context menu on state changes, and routes menu clicks to action, toggle-window, and quit callbacks.

nodes.name: makeTemplateImage
nodes.summary: Builds a template nativeImage from base64 1x and 2x PNG payloads so the tray icon renders crisply and adapts to the menu-bar appearance.

nodes.name: anthropic.ts
nodes.summary: Anthropic Messages API provider implementation using Node's built-in fetch (no vendor SDK), exposing testConnection and a non-streaming complete() with content-free, status-derived error messages.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the LlmProvider interface from provider.ts; deliberately avoids the Anthropic SDK to keep egress small and auditable (ADR-0029).

nodes.name: AnthropicProvider
nodes.summary: LlmProvider for api.anthropic.com using x-api-key auth; implements testConnection and complete(), extracting assistant text from the Messages response and mapping non-ok HTTP to status-derived errors.

nodes.name: cloud-log.ts
nodes.summary: Persists a rolling, metadata-only activity log of cloud/local LLM calls to app data via atomic rename, capped at a max entry count so transcript content is never written.
nodes.languageNotes: Atomic writes via temp-file + fs.renameSync; entries are coerced through normalizeEntry to tolerate older/garbage on-disk shapes (ADR-0031 §4).

nodes.name: appendCloudCall
nodes.summary: Appends one CloudCallLogEntry, trims the log to its capacity, and writes it back atomically, swallowing errors so logging never breaks an LLM call.

nodes.name: normalizeEntry
nodes.summary: Coerces an untrusted on-disk value into a well-formed CloudCallLogEntry, defaulting missing or malformed fields so reads never throw.

nodes.name: readFile
nodes.summary: Reads and parses the cloud-log file from disk, tolerating a missing or corrupt file by returning an empty entry list and normalizing each entry.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Orchestrator for all main-process LLM operations: config/key management, summarize, whole-transcript and per-segment translation, this-meeting/vault Q&A, enforcing the redact-before-cloud and metadata-only logging egress discipline.
nodes.languageNotes: All LLM calls originate here in the Electron main process (ADR-0029); cloud egress is redacted and logged, local (loopback) egress is full-text with all-zero redaction (ADR-0031).

nodes.name: summarize
nodes.summary: Produces a markdown meeting summary: redacts the transcript for cloud egress (full-text for local), calls the configured provider, and appends a metadata-only cloud-log entry.

nodes.name: translate
nodes.summary: Translates an assembled transcript into a target language via the configured provider, applying the same redact-on-cloud / full-on-local egress discipline and logging.

nodes.name: translateSegment
nodes.summary: Translates a single finalized live segment to a target language, redacting the line on cloud, and records it into an aggregated live-translate roll-up rather than logging per call.

nodes.name: ask
nodes.summary: Answers a user question grounded in either the meeting transcript or retrieved vault chunks, redacting both the question and each grounding text for cloud egress and logging metadata only.

nodes.name: recordLiveTranslate
nodes.summary: Accumulates per-segment live-translation metadata into a rolling aggregate, flushing it to the cloud log when the provider/egress changes so the 500-entry log isn't flooded.

nodes.name: setConfig
nodes.summary: Validates untrusted IPC config input, persists the non-secret LLM config to prefs.json, and returns the recomputed status.

nodes.name: testConnection
nodes.summary: Decrypts the stored key, builds the configured provider, and runs its cheap live validation call, returning a content-free ok/detail result.

nodes.name: logCloudCall
nodes.summary: Builds a timestamped, metadata-only CloudCallLogEntry from call parameters and appends it to the persistent cloud-call log.

nodes.name: isLocalEgress
nodes.summary: Determines whether a config's endpoint is a loopback (localhost) target, which means zero egress and skips redaction.

nodes.name: keystore.ts
nodes.summary: Per-provider API key store encrypting secrets at rest via Electron safeStorage, persisted with restrictive file permissions; the plaintext key never crosses the contextBridge (ADR-0030).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Electron safeStorage.encryptString/decryptString; writes are atomic (temp + chmod 0600 + rename) and gated on isEncryptionAvailable.

nodes.name: getKey
nodes.summary: Decrypts and returns the stored API key for a provider via safeStorage, returning undefined when no key exists or encryption is unavailable.

nodes.name: setKey
nodes.summary: Encrypts a provider's API key via safeStorage and writes it to the on-disk store, throwing KeyStorageUnavailableError when OS encryption is not available.

nodes.name: readStore
nodes.summary: Reads and parses the encrypted key store from disk, tolerating a missing or corrupt file by returning an empty store.

nodes.name: writeStore
nodes.summary: Persists the key store atomically with 0600 permissions (temp-file write, chmod, rename) so secrets are never world-readable mid-write.

nodes.name: KeyStorageUnavailableError
nodes.summary: Error thrown when OS-level encryption (safeStorage) is unavailable, signaling that an API key cannot be securely stored.

nodes.name: openai-compatible.ts
nodes.summary: OpenAI-compatible chat-completions provider over a configurable baseUrl, covering cloud endpoints (OpenAI/Gemini/OpenRouter) and local loopback servers (Ollama/LM Studio/llama.cpp) with optional auth.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements LlmProvider from provider.ts using fetch only; local loopback baseUrls need no key, enabling a zero-egress path.

nodes.name: OpenAiCompatibleProvider
nodes.summary: LlmProvider targeting any /v1/chat/completions-style endpoint; normalizes the base URL, runs testConnection against the models endpoint, and performs a non-streaming complete() with status-derived errors.

nodes.name: provider.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the LlmProvider abstraction (testConnection/complete/stream), the shared request/result types, network timeout constants, and a factory that builds the concrete provider from config.
nodes.languageNotes: makeProvider uses lazy require() of the two implementations to avoid a circular import, since each impl imports the LlmProvider interface from here.

nodes.name: makeProvider
nodes.summary: Factory that constructs the concrete LlmProvider (Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible) from the config and optional decrypted key, using lazy requires to break a circular import.

nodes.name: detailForStatus
nodes.summary: Maps a numeric HTTP status to a short, content-free, human-readable detail string so error messages never leak response bodies or secrets.

nodes.name: redaction.ts
nodes.summary: PII redactor that collapses emails, phones, money, numbers, URLs, and known roster names to category placeholders before cloud egress, returning the redacted text plus per-category counts.
nodes.languageNotes: Each detector is a regex pass; known names are escaped and sorted longest-first before substitution to avoid partial-name collisions.

nodes.name: redact
nodes.summary: Runs the category detectors plus known-name substitution over input text and returns the redacted string with a per-category and total count of replacements.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Locked main-process IPC contract for the LLM subsystem: provider config/status, summarize/translate/ask request and result shapes, redaction counts, and the metadata-only cloud-call log entry.
nodes.languageNotes: Source of truth the sandboxed renderer mirrors; the API key never appears in any shape — the renderer only learns hasKey: boolean (ADR-0030).

nodes.name: angular.json
nodes.summary: Angular CLI workspace config for the hark-ui renderer: defines the application build target (browser entry src/main.ts, output dist/renderer, zone.js polyfill) plus production budgets and a dev-server, with standalone OnPush components and analytics disabled.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the modern @angular/build:application builder (esbuild-based) rather than the legacy webpack browser builder.

nodes.name: electron-builder.yml
nodes.summary: electron-builder packaging config that produces a signed, notarization-ready macOS .app/dmg/zip for arm64, bundling the compiled renderer+main and the statically-linked harkd Swift sidecar, with hardened runtime, inherit-entitlement signing of the sidecar, and TCC usage strings — no auto-update, no publish, no telemetry.
nodes.languageNotes: The mac.binaries entry explicitly re-signs the extraResources-copied harkd so it inherits cs.inherit entitlements (electron-builder's deep-sign pass skips Contents/Resources/), which is load-bearing for the audio-capture TCC grant to attribute to Hark and for notarization.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: npm manifest for the Electron + Angular 21 UI shell: declares the compiled Electron main entry (dist/main/main.js), Angular/RxJS runtime deps and Electron/electron-builder dev deps, and orchestrates the build/dev/dist scripts that compile the engine, renderer, and main process.
nodes.languageNotes: The dist/pack scripts run `build:engine` (swift build -c release) before packaging so the bundled harkd sidecar is never stale.

nodes.name: tsconfig.app.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript project config for the Angular renderer build: extends the base tsconfig, compiles src/app and src/main.ts, and explicitly excludes the Electron main-process sources under src/main.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: Base TypeScript compiler config for the UI workspace, enabling strict mode and Angular template strictness (strictTemplates, strictInjectionParameters) with ES2022 modules and bundler resolution for the renderer.

nodes.name: tsconfig.main.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript config for the Electron main process: compiles src/main/**/*.ts to CommonJS in dist/main with strict mode and Node types, separate from the Angular renderer toolchain.

nodes.name: HarkCaptureCLI.swift
nodes.summary: Entry point for the hark-capture CLI: an AsyncParsableCommand that gates permissions, builds a CapturePipeline from --mic-only/--system-only/--output flags, and stops cleanly on SIGINT or an optional --duration timer.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses @main + swift-argument-parser's AsyncParsableCommand; coordinates SIGINT and the duration timer through a single CheckedContinuation guarded by a one-shot resume helper.

nodes.name: HarkCapture
nodes.summary: AsyncParsableCommand struct defining the hark-capture flags and run() logic — permission preflight/request, mutual-exclusion validation, pipeline start/stop, and final stats reporting.

nodes.name: OneShotResume
nodes.summary: Lock-guarded helper that resumes a CheckedContinuation exactly once so the SIGINT source and duration timer can race without double-resuming.

nodes.name: HarkPaths.swift
nodes.summary: Single authoritative resolver for Hark's rebuildable app-data directories (~/Library/Application Support/Hark, its Models/ and index/ subdirs), enforcing CLAUDE.md hard rule #2 that caches never land in the vault.

nodes.name: HarkPaths
nodes.summary: Namespace enum with appSupportDir()/modelsDir()/indexDir() static helpers that create-if-missing the sanctioned app-support locations for model and vault-RAG index data.

nodes.name: Heartbeat.swift
nodes.summary: Provides startHeartbeat(), a cancellable background Task that prints an elapsed-time ticker to stderr while long no-progress steps (like ANE compile) run.

nodes.name: startHeartbeat
nodes.summary: Starts a cancellable Task that writes "[ N s elapsed ] <label>..." to the given FileHandle on a fixed interval until cancelled.

nodes.name: ModelLoader.swift
nodes.summary: Shared two-phase WhisperKit loader: downloads model files with a progress bar (Phase A) then prewarms/compiles to the ANE with a heartbeat and structured progress pulses (Phase B), returning a timed LoadedModel.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges WhisperKit's Foundation Progress callback and a @Sendable structured-progress sink; an indeterminate 'optimizing' pulse re-emits every ~1.5s during the no-progress ANE compile.

nodes.name: loadWhisperKit
nodes.summary: Async function that downloads (with ProgressRenderer) then compiles+loads a WhisperKit pipeline, forwarding both stderr progress and an optional structured onProgress sink for the harkd UI.

nodes.name: LoadedModel
nodes.summary: Result struct returned by loadWhisperKit carrying the WhisperKit pipe, model name/folder, and download/compile/total load timings.

nodes.name: ProgressRenderer.swift
nodes.summary: Terminal progress bar that updates in place via carriage return, rendering percent plus MB/throughput/ETA when byte counts are available, throttled to ~10 redraws/sec via a serial queue.

nodes.name: ProgressRenderer
nodes.summary: Final @unchecked Sendable class consuming Foundation Progress from any thread, serializing redraws through a DispatchQueue and distinguishing byte-count vs opaque-unit progress.

nodes.name: WAVWriter.swift
nodes.summary: Streaming WAV writer for 16 kHz mono Int16 PCM: emits a placeholder RIFF header, appends samples as they arrive, then seeks back and patches the two size fields on close.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses FileHandle seek-and-patch (RandomAccessFile analogue); little-endian size fields written via withUnsafeBytes; deinit closes idempotently.

nodes.name: WAVWriter
nodes.summary: Final class managing a streaming WAV file: init writes the 44-byte header, append() writes Int16 LE samples, and close() patches RIFF/data sizes idempotently.

nodes.name: convert-embedder-coreml.py
nodes.summary: Build-time script that converts intfloat/multilingual-e5-small to a CoreML .mlpackage (flexible 1..512 sequence length) for Hark's vault-RAG embedder and saves the tokenizer files alongside.
nodes.languageNotes: Wraps the HF model to expose only last_hidden_state, traces with torch.jit, and converts via coremltools with a RangeDim for variable sequence length targeting CPU_AND_NE.

nodes.name: Wrap
nodes.summary: torch.nn.Module wrapper that exposes only the embedder's last_hidden_state output, leaving masked-mean-pooling and L2-normalization to the Swift loader.

nodes.name: hark-tap.entitlements
nodes.summary: Code-signing entitlements granting com.apple.security.device.audio-input, used when signing the dev capture bundle for the Core Audio Process Tap path.

nodes.name: publish-embedder-hf.sh
nodes.summary: One-time deploy script that uploads the int8 CoreML embedder + tokenizer to a HuggingFace repo and reports the commit SHA to pin in EmbedderModels.swift, so the engine can fetch the model at first run.

nodes.name: quantize-embedder-int8.py
nodes.summary: Linearly quantizes the fp16 CoreML embedder weights to int8 (halving the download), copies the tokenizer alongside, and validates cross-lingual fidelity via fp16-vs-int8 embedding cosine before shipping.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses coremltools.optimize per-channel symmetric int8 quantization and mirrors Hark's Swift masked-mean-pool + L2-normalize to compute a faithful fidelity score.

nodes.name: size_mb
nodes.summary: Walks an .mlpackage directory and sums file sizes to report the model package size in megabytes.

nodes.name: embed
nodes.summary: Tokenizes text, runs the CoreML model, and returns a masked-mean-pooled, L2-normalized embedding matching Hark's Swift pooling for the fidelity check.

nodes.name: sign-dev-bundle.sh
nodes.summary: Wraps an SPM-built engine binary (hark-capture or harkd) in a minimal signed .app bundle with NSAudioCaptureUsageDescription so Core Audio Process Taps can acquire and retain the kTCCServiceAudioCapture grant.

nodes.name: .understandignore
nodes.summary: Gitignore-style exclude list for the Understand-Anything analyzer; scopes the scan to code by excluding build artifacts (.build/, .angular/) and all docs/markdown.

nodes.name: config.json
nodes.summary: Single-key config for the Understand-Anything analyzer, setting the output language to English.

nodes.name: Package.swift
nodes.summary: Swift Package Manager manifest for the Hark engine, declaring four executables (hark-bench, hark-engine, hark-capture, harkd) plus the HarkCore/HarkCapture libraries and pinning WhisperKit, swift-nio, FluidAudio, swift-transformers, and swift-crypto.
nodes.languageNotes: SPM manifest is itself Swift code; dependencies are pinned exactly or by SemVer range with inline rationale tied to ADRs and privacy rules.

nodes.name: .gitkeep
nodes.summary: Empty placeholder that keeps the engine/Results/ directory (where HarkBench writes RTF benchmark JSON) tracked in git.

nodes.name: main.swift
nodes.summary: Phase 0 Real-Time-Factor harness binary: loads WhisperKit, slides a 30s/5s-hop window over an input audio file, measures per-window transcription wall-clock, and emits a PASS/FAIL RTF report as JSON to stdout and engine/Results/.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses top-level code in main.swift (implicit @main); Codable structs with snake_case key-encoding strategy produce the report JSON.

nodes.name: detectChip
nodes.summary: Shells out to sysctl machdep.cpu.brand_string to read the Apple Silicon chip name for the benchmark hardware report.

nodes.name: percentile
nodes.summary: Computes a percentile of a Double array via linear interpolation between ranks; used for RTF p50/p95/p99 stats.

nodes.name: gitShortSha
nodes.summary: Runs git rev-parse --short HEAD against the repo to stamp the benchmark result filename, falling back to "nogit" on any failure.

nodes.name: CapturePipeline.swift
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the capture path: mic + system-audio backends → per-source Resampler → FIFO → 100ms pump → Mixer → optional WAV writer and Float-frame streaming sink for harkd.
nodes.languageNotes: FIFO drain uses an NSLock and a DispatchSourceTimer pump; FIFO append is keyed by ReferenceWritableKeyPath. Backend selected at runtime via the SystemAudioCapturing existential.

nodes.name: CapturePipeline
nodes.summary: Final class that wires mic/system capture to resampling, FIFO buffering, a 100ms pump, soft-clipping mix, and WAV/streaming sinks; emits a per-second JSON heartbeat with underrun and peak stats.

nodes.name: Options
nodes.summary: Configuration struct for CapturePipeline: which sources to capture, optional WAV output URL, optional Float-frame sink, and pump/underrun frame sizes.

nodes.name: CoreAudioProcessTap.swift
nodes.summary: Selectable (HARK_CAPTURE_BACKEND=tap) system-audio backend using macOS 14.4+ Core Audio Process Taps: builds a global tap + private aggregate device, runs a dedicated CFRunLoop for HAL notifications, and delivers PCM buffers from a realtime IOProc.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy C-style HAL interop (AudioObjectID property reads, CFRunLoop, dlopen TCC SPI via PermissionGate); IOProc block avoids touching self on the realtime thread.

nodes.name: CoreAudioProcessTap
nodes.summary: SystemAudioCapturing implementation over Core Audio Process Taps; manages tap/aggregate/IOProc lifecycle, a dedicated HAL run loop, and TCC audio-capture permission, with extensive HARK_TAP_DEBUG diagnostics.

nodes.name: MicCapture.swift
nodes.summary: Microphone capture via AVAudioEngine: installs a tap on the input node and forwards native-format PCM buffers to a caller closure on the Core Audio thread.

nodes.name: MicCapture
nodes.summary: Final class wrapping an AVAudioEngine input tap; exposes the native source format and start/stop that deliver AVAudioPCMBuffers to a BufferHandler.

nodes.name: Mixer.swift
nodes.summary: Sums two 16 kHz mono Float32 streams, applies tanh soft-clip, scales to Int16, and tracks frames-written / per-source underrun / peak-amplitude stats.

nodes.name: Mixer
nodes.summary: Final class that mixes one aligned chunk from each enabled source into Int16 PCM, counting underruns only for enabled-but-missing sources and updating Stats.

nodes.name: PermissionGate.swift
nodes.summary: TCC permission gate for capture: pure preflight checks plus active requests for Microphone and Screen Recording, and a dev-only private-SPI path (dlopen TCC) for the kTCCServiceAudioCapture permission behind HARK_ENABLE_TCC_SPI.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges async permission callbacks with withCheckedContinuation; the private-API section resolves TCCAccessPreflight/TCCAccessRequest by symbol name via dlopen/dlsym.

nodes.name: PermissionGate
nodes.summary: Namespace enum exposing check(), ensureGranted(), requestMicrophone(), and the dev-only private-SPI audio-capture preflight/request used by the Core Audio tap path.

nodes.name: Status
nodes.summary: Value struct holding mic/screen grant flags with derived allGranted and an exit code; an extension prints a human-readable report with remediation steps.

nodes.name: Resampler.swift
nodes.summary: Wraps AVAudioConverter to convert arbitrary-input PCM to 16 kHz mono Float32, sizing the output buffer generously and reporting the actual converted frame count.

nodes.name: Resampler
nodes.summary: Final class wrapping AVAudioConverter; failable init builds the 16 kHz mono target, and convert() handles rate conversion and channel downmix per buffer.

nodes.name: SystemAudioCapturing.swift
nodes.summary: Protocol abstracting the two system-audio backends (ScreenCaptureKit SystemAudioTap and Core Audio CoreAudioProcessTap) so CapturePipeline can swap them via a one-line factory change.
nodes.languageNotes: An AnyObject-constrained protocol used as an existential (`any SystemAudioCapturing`) — Swift's equivalent of a Java interface-typed field selected at runtime.

nodes.name: SystemAudioCapturing
nodes.summary: Protocol declaring sourceFormat plus start(onBuffer:)/stop() — the seam both system-audio capture backends conform to.

nodes.name: SystemAudioTap.swift
nodes.summary: Default system-audio backend using ScreenCaptureKit (SCStream): captures audio under the Screen Recording TCC grant by running a deliberately tiny no-op video stream and copying audio CMSampleBuffers to AVAudioPCMBuffers.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges SCK's async setup to a sync start() via DispatchSemaphore; conforms to NSObject + SCStreamOutput; copies samples with CMSampleBufferCopyPCMDataIntoAudioBufferList to outlive the callback.

nodes.name: SystemAudioTap
nodes.summary: SCStreamOutput-conforming SystemAudioCapturing backend that configures an audio+minimal-video SCStream, latches the delivered format on the first buffer, and forwards copied PCM buffers to the handler.

layers.name: Engine Core & Audio Capture
layers.description: Swift HarkCore primitives plus the ScreenCaptureKit / Core Audio Process Tap pipeline (HarkCapture, its CLI, and HarkBench) that pulls system + mic audio on-device.

layers.name: Streaming Daemon & Transcription
layers.description: The harkd sidecar: loopback WebSocket server, session/wire protocol, VAD, WhisperKit ASR and FluidAudio diarization that turn captured audio into segment frames.

layers.name: Engine Tests
layers.description: Swift Testing suites covering the engine — capture, VAD, transcription, diarization, and the harkd wire protocol.

layers.name: UI Renderer (Angular)
layers.description: Angular 21 renderer: components, services, the WebSocket client to harkd, and renderer entry/styles that present live captions, translation, and the second-brain UI.

layers.name: Electron Main Process
layers.description: Electron main process — window/tray management, preload bridges, harkd spawning, port-file handshake, and preferences persistence.

layers.name: Privacy & LLM Egress
layers.description: The only sanctioned network path off the machine: local RAG (loopback MCP/HTTP) and the LLM provider clients with redaction, keystore, and cloud-egress logging for summary/translation/Q&A.

layers.name: Build & Configuration
layers.description: Project build and tooling — Swift Package manifest, signing/notarization and CoreML conversion scripts, Angular/Electron/TypeScript/Tailwind configs, and knowledge-graph settings.

tour.title: App Launch: Electron Main
tour.description: The story starts where the user double-clicks the app. The Electron main process bootstraps everything: it ensures the local vault directory exists, spawns the Swift harkd sidecar, creates the main BrowserWindow and the menu-bar tray, and registers the IPC handlers that bridge the renderer to native capabilities. This single file is the trust boundary between the sandboxed UI and the privileged engine, so reading it first frames how Hark stays local-first.
tour.languageLesson: Electron splits into a main process (Node.js, full OS access) and a renderer (the Angular UI in a Chromium window). They can only talk through IPC channels declared in main.ts and exposed via a preload bridge — the renderer never gets raw Node APIs.

tour.title: Spawning the Engine Sidecar
tour.description: Hark's engine is not in-process — it is a separate signed Swift binary supervised as a child process. harkd-spawn resolves the signed binary path and launches it, then waits on the port file before reporting readiness, while port-file polls the JSON port file that harkd writes once its WebSocket is listening. This handshake is why the UI and engine can be signed, sandboxed, and crash-isolated independently.
tour.languageLesson: The port file is a rendezvous pattern: rather than hard-coding a port (which could collide), the child picks a free port at bind time and writes it to a known file as JSON. The parent polls that file with a timeout — a simple, race-free way to discover a dynamically-bound server.

tour.title: The harkd Daemon Entry Point
tour.description: Now we cross into Swift. HarkdCommand is the daemon's entry point and the engine's highest-scoring entry candidate: it binds the loopback-only WebSocket server and writes the engine.port file FIRST, then loads WhisperKit behind it so the UI can connect immediately and watch model-loading progress stream in. The WebSocketServer underneath runs on SwiftNIO, binds to localhost only, performs the WS upgrade, and carries one JSON object per frame with 5-second heartbeats. Loopback-only binding is a hard privacy guarantee, not a default.
tour.languageLesson: harkd is built with Swift ArgumentParser's @main command pattern (analogous to a Spring Boot @SpringBootApplication main). SwiftNIO is an event-loop networking framework — like Netty in the JVM world — so the server is non-blocking and channel-based rather than thread-per-connection.

tour.title: Engine Build & Dependency Map
tour.description: Before following the audio path, see how the engine is assembled. Package.swift is the Swift Package Manager manifest declaring four executables (harkd, hark-engine, hark-capture, hark-bench) plus the HarkCore and HarkCapture libraries, and it pins WhisperKit and FluidAudio. This is the engine's architecture in one file: the capture library, the core utilities, and the daemon that stitches them together — exactly the layers we walk next.
tour.languageLesson: Package.swift is Swift's equivalent of pom.xml or build.gradle, but it is itself executable Swift code, not declarative XML. Targets map to folders under Sources/, and a target's dependencies list controls what it can import — the compiler enforces the module boundaries you declare here.

tour.title: Capturing & Mixing Audio
tour.description: This is where sound enters the system. CapturePipeline orchestrates the whole path: it pulls microphone audio (MicCapture, an AVAudioEngine tap) and system audio (SystemAudioTap, a ScreenCaptureKit stream that copies audio under the Screen Recording grant), resamples each source to 16 kHz, then hands both to the Mixer, which sums them, soft-clips with tanh, and scales to Int16. PermissionGate is the bouncer that preflights and requests the Microphone and Screen Recording TCC grants before any of this runs. Two messy real-world audio sources become one clean 16 kHz mono stream ready for ASR.
tour.languageLesson: Audio callbacks fire on a real-time Core Audio thread where you must never block, allocate, or lock. MicCapture forwards buffers to a caller closure on that thread, so the pipeline downstream of it uses lock-free FIFOs and a separate pump to move data off the audio thread safely.

tour.title: Loading the WhisperKit Model
tour.description: ASR needs a model on the Apple Neural Engine. ModelLoader is the shared two-phase WhisperKit loader: Phase A downloads the model files with a progress bar, Phase B prewarms and compiles them to the ANE while emitting structured progress pulses — those pulses are what the UI's model-loading screen renders. HarkPaths is the single authoritative resolver for Hark's rebuildable app-data directories, enforcing the hard rule that nothing model- or cache-related is written outside Application Support/Hark. Together they answer 'where do models live, and how do we load them without freezing the UI?'

tour.title: Transcription: VAD, Window, Finalize
tour.description: EngineSession is the heart of the engine — the central actor that wires Capture to VAD to SlidingWindow to WhisperKit to the WebSocket emit, with backpressure, dedup, diarization, and the vault-save lifecycle. VAD gates which frames count as speech so silence never enters the window. SlidingWindow runs a 30-second window with a 5-second hop and an UtteranceLedger that reconciles repeatedly re-transcribed audio into stable utterance identities (ADR-0008/0009/0019) — this is what stops captions from flickering and rewriting themselves. This is the engine's most-depended-on orchestration file.
tour.languageLesson: EngineSession is a Swift actor: the language serializes access to its mutable state so concurrent callbacks from the audio thread, the WhisperKit task, and the WebSocket can't race. It's the structured-concurrency answer to a synchronized service class in Java — but the compiler enforces the isolation.

tour.title: The Wire Protocol Contract
tour.description: The engine and UI are two processes in two languages, so the contract between them is sacred. WireProtocol defines the JSON envelope and every Codable payload — every engine-to-UI event and UI-to-engine command — on the Swift side. engine.types.ts is the TypeScript mirror of that same contract on the renderer side, plus shared constants like LANGUAGE_CHOICES. Keeping these two files in lockstep (snake_case on the wire) is the whole reason the harkd↔UI integration stays correct; this is the seam everything else hangs off.
tour.languageLesson: Swift's Codable auto-derives JSON encode/decode from struct shape, while TypeScript interfaces only describe shape at compile time. Neither side validates the other at runtime, so a frame truly exists only when the Swift struct and the TS interface agree — which is why Hark has a dedicated skill to edit both ends together.

tour.title: Live Captions in the Renderer
tour.description: Back in the UI, engine.service is the renderer's hub and its single most-imported service: the WebSocket client that connects to harkd, parses every wire frame (hello, ready, model progress, heartbeat, capture, segment, bookmark, meeting-saved) and re-exposes them as Angular signals. app.component is the shell with the highest fan-out in the whole codebase — it orchestrates capture controls, the transcript, and every overlay panel by wiring engine, LLM, preferences, and retrieval services together. transcript-line renders one caption: timestamp, speaker color chip, text, optional translation, and the partial-typing caret. Building on Step 8's contract, this is where wire frames become pixels.
tour.languageLesson: Angular 21 signals are reactive values: engine.service exposes connection state and incoming segments as signals, and templates re-render automatically when a signal changes — no manual change detection, no RxJS subscription bookkeeping for this state. It's pull-based reactivity, the modern replacement for BehaviorSubject-everywhere.

tour.title: Identity, Theme & Status Surface
tour.description: Hark's recent UI work gives the shell a native, branded feel rather than generic Electron chrome. The ripples component draws the 'Heard ripples' identity motif — concentric accent rings and a pulsing core, pure CSS-over-SVG — and it is shared across the shell's resting and active states (it has high fan-in among UI components for a reason). tokens.css is the central design-token sheet: every color, font, radius, and the status/speaker palettes live here under light and dark themes, so theme switching is a single attribute flip. status-banner is the presentational surface that renders status and warning messages with severity-driven color. This is the layer that makes captions feel like a product, not a console.
tour.languageLesson: Design tokens are CSS custom properties (variables) scoped to [data-theme] selectors; Tailwind utilities reference them via var(), so no concrete color value is ever hard-coded in a component. Switching theme = changing one attribute on the document root, and the whole UI re-resolves through the cascade.

tour.title: On Stop: Diarize, Save, Enroll
tour.description: When capture stops, a heavier off-line pass runs so it never burdens the live path. Diarizer wraps FluidAudio's offline manager to segment the whole meeting, embed each segment, and cluster speakers (VBx) in one serialized pass. SpeakerEnrollment is the local voiceprint store (ADR-0026): it persists a named speaker's centroid and auto-recognizes that voice in future meetings via cosine distance — and those embeddings never leave the machine. VaultWriter then renders the finished meeting to markdown with front-matter and blockquoted utterances and git-commits it. This trio turns a live stream into a durable, attributed, recoverable note.
tour.languageLesson: Diarization (who spoke) is decoupled from transcription (what was said) on purpose: running clustering live would add latency and instability, so Hark does it once at capture.stop. The vault write is a git commit, making every change to the user's notes auditable and reversible — the vault is treated as sacred state.

tour.title: The Vault Second Brain: Local RAG
tour.description: Saved meetings become a searchable second brain — entirely on-device. RagIndexer coordinates the vault index: a cold build on open, FSEvents-driven debounced re-indexing as notes change, and graceful degradation if the embedder is missing. TextEmbedder is the on-device CoreML embedder (tokenize, ANE inference, masked mean-pooling, L2-normalize to a 384-dim vector, fully offline). RagIndex is a brute-force in-memory cosine vector store persisted as flat files. retrieval.service in the renderer is the thin router that resolves a query either through this built-in engine path or an external RAG bridge. No cloud vector DB, no embeddings API — retrieval is local by construction.

tour.title: The Only Network Egress
tour.description: Everything so far stayed on the Mac. The single deliberate exception is the cloud-LLM path, and Hark fences it carefully. llm/index orchestrates summarize, translate, and Q&A and enforces the redact-before-send rule; redaction collapses emails, phones, money, numbers, URLs, and known roster names to category placeholders before any text leaves; provider abstracts each cloud backend behind a testConnection/complete/stream interface with strict network timeouts; and rag/loopback asserts that even a configured RAG endpoint resolves to a loopback host before any fetch (ADR-0034). This step is the privacy thesis of the whole project, expressed in code.
tour.languageLesson: Cloud egress lives only in the Electron main process, never the renderer — the UI must ask main to make the call, so there is one auditable choke point. The provider factory is a strategy pattern: index.ts depends on the LlmProvider interface, and a factory swaps Anthropic vs. OpenAI-compatible backends behind it, keeping the redaction-and-timeout policy provider-agnostic.

tour.title: Packaging the App
tour.description: Finally, how does all of this ship as one double-clickable Mac app? electron-builder.yml is the packaging config that produces a signed, notarization-ready .app/.dmg/.zip for arm64, bundling the compiled renderer and main process together with the statically-linked harkd Swift binary. This is the capstone: the two-process, two-language architecture you toured — Electron UI plus Swift engine — collapses into a single signed artifact the user installs, with the engine spawned exactly as we saw in Step 2.
tour.languageLesson: macOS gatekeeping requires the .app to be code-signed and notarized (stapled by Apple) or it won't launch for end users. electron-builder bundles the Swift sidecar as a resource inside the .app so the whole thing — UI and engine — is signed and notarized as one unit; the harness's smoke/test skills wrap binaries in signed bundles for the same TCC reason.
